correctness.rationale: The joint probabilities are reconstructed separately for j>i, j=i and j<i by conditional relative-order symmetry, maximum-of-prefix distribution and a binomial hockey-stick sum. Exact covariances follow after subtracting marginals. Row and column identities use finite telescoping sums, all boundary signs are algebraic, and strict aggregate monotonicity follows from decreasing reciprocal-binomial terms. The packaged exact verifier passed 640 checks including exhaustive enumerations through n=8. The all-n proof does not rely on that enumeration.

originality.rationale: After explicit primary-source comparisons and targeted index searches, no result was found stating or directly implying the complete record-position versus excedance-position covariance matrix. Important distinction: Sokal–Zeng (2020) already supplies a stronger aggregate generating function for record and excedance counts, so the total covariance and its sign reversal are not independently claimed novel. Their unindexed count-polynomial does not directly yield the pairwise absolute-position entries or the row/column sign laws. Older positional refinements remain a genuine risk.

value.rationale: The matrix is a complete and naturally indexed dependence classification for the interaction of the classical Stirling record statistic and Eulerian excedance statistic under a uniform permutation law. It reveals a directional zero/negative/positive pattern not visible in aggregate generating functions, yields different exact row and column sign boundaries, and clarifies the finite-size aggregate sign crossover. A positional covariance law is a motivated structural refinement of the established joint-statistics literature rather than an arbitrary table cell.
